brief: GS argues that $100 Brent sits atop roughly $20–25/bbl of risk premium rather than a current physical shortage: Gulf exports have normalized, inventories sit above early-2025 levels, and GS sees September as roughly balanced. The buffer has changed instead of the barrels: ex-OECD commercial inventories are near record lows and spare capacity is less certain, so the tail risk is another attack cutting Gulf flows back below 50% with a much thinner cushion to absorb it, even though GS says stocks remain comfortably above operational minimums. That is why $100 oil can coexist with a balanced market. Yet oil options do not reflect this fear: OVX trades near the levels it held when oil was below $80, unlike February/March when rising oil brought a sharp vol repricing. Call skew has moved back toward pre-war levels, the options bid is concentrated in puts, and macro funds exposed to another spike are buying outright delta rather than upside calls. Flat price is pricing geopolitical fear, upside vol is not, and the note says one of the two eventually has to move.
